object_description: multi-part two-storey volume with a backbone and offset wings
design_condition: The building's main volume runs parallel to the highway as a noise-protective backbone, while offset volumes settle into the landslide topography and frame differentiated outdoor spaces around the slope and rock formation.

positive.statement: The figure of several building parts reacts convincingly to the unsettled topography caused by the landslide.

position.rationale: Multiple offset parts, backbone and wings are clearly legible across the top and elevations.

positive.statement: The main volume provides noise protection for the outdoor spaces behind it.

position.rationale: The long parallel backbone dominates the footprint and forms repeated horizontal elevation bands.

positive.statement: The volumes engage with the slope edge and striking rock formation, creating an interaction with the morphology of the place.

position.rationale: Terrain and rock are not distinct point-cloud elements; the anchor follows the offset landscape-facing edge.

positive.statement: The landscaped right of way leads through a park-like green space to the covered access situation.

position.target: landscaped right of way and covered access
position.rationale: Access is approximated at the low front-left edge of the articulated footprint.

positive.statement: The formation of the building structure connects differentiated and well-oriented open spaces with the interior organization.

position.rationale: Outdoor spaces are represented by the gaps and recesses between offset building parts.

positive.statement: The two-storey volume sits relatively reservedly in the landscape and organizes the school facilities in a child-friendly manner.

position.rationale: Two-storey massing and reserved landscape placement are clear in all elevations.

positive.statement: The shifted sections make corridors narrow and expand in interesting ways, providing clear views of the surrounding landscape.

position.rationale: Corridors are interior; the estimate follows the central shifted junction of the volumes.

positive.statement: The upper level is well ventilated away from the noise, while the lower rooms are protected by the existing earth wall.

position.target: upper level ventilation and lower earth-wall protection
position.rationale: Upper and lower levels are visible, while ventilation and earth-wall conditions remain inferred.

positive.statement: The pent roof brings additional light into the depth of the rooms and breaks up the volume.

position.rationale: The roofed articulated profile is visible as the upper edge and stepped silhouette.

positive.statement: The project blends unobtrusively yet spectacularly into the landscape, with a sufficiently strong building expression.

position.rationale: Overall integration and articulated expression are represented by the complete sampled building.

positive.statement: Low volume requirements, a simple support system and minor topographic interventions enable economical implementation.

position.rationale: Economy is non-geometric; marker approximates the simple, low-rise primary volume.

negative.statement: The entrance is somewhat set back and cramped within the terrain formation.

position.rationale: Entrance is not identifiable; constrained to the recessed low front edge.

negative.statement: The proposed disposition of the two kindergarten rooms cannot be combined.

position.rationale: Interior rooms are absent; estimate placed in the lower central building zone.

negative.statement: The reception is somewhat decentralized and cannot be found immediately from the main entrance.

position.rationale: Reception is not visible; location is constrained near the likely main access edge.

negative.statement: The wheelchair-accessible ramps are very long, so the access theme is overused and requires a lot of space.

position.rationale: Ramps are absent from the sample; marker follows the low frontage and access approach.

negative.statement: The separation of vertical access for fire safety reasons would be difficult and complex, and additional emergency exits are required.

position.rationale: Fire circulation is interior; the anchor uses the central vertical organization.

negative.statement: The relatively high level of building development has a negative impact on operation and gray energy.

position.rationale: Operational and embodied-energy criticism has no useful single geometric location.

negative.statement: The proposed insulation for the ground-floor overhang is not sufficient for the MINERGIE-P standard.

position.rationale: Insulation is not visible; estimate follows the lower overhanging edge.

negative.statement: The wet cells are only partially grouped, and unresolved technology shafts will reduce usable areas.

position.rationale: Interior service grouping is absent; marker uses the central service-bearing portion of the building.
